podcast.title: Pioneering West Coast Smooth Blues
podcast.body: In the late 1940s and early 1950s, the Nat King Cole Trio was one of the biggest groups in the R&B field, popularizing a smooth blues style that incorporated elements of crooning alongside blues and jazz. Their style was highly influential on the burgeoning rock music field, with groups like the Chuck Berry Trio attempting to emulate it. "Two of the biggest groups in the Iron B field were the Nat King Colds' Rio and Johnny Moore's three blazers featuring Charles Brown."

podcast.title: Pre-Pop Ballad Influence
podcast.body: Before Nat King Cole achieved massive pop success with ballads like "Unforgettable," the music he made with his trio, while perhaps not as commercially successful, was incredibly influential on the developing rock music scene. "But it's still hard for modern listeners to remember that before his massive pop success with ballads like unforgettable, Cold was making music, which may not have been quite as successful commercially, but which was incredibly influential on the burgeoning rock music field."
